<description>
Add a test that sends one address too far in the future and one too old and check addrman stores both as 5 days old.

The future-timestamp clamp is the only guard against a peer rewriting existing addrman entries with far-future times, which would make them permanently terrible.

Kills the following mutants:

```diff
diff --git a/src/net_processing.cpp b/src/net_processing.cpp
index e25a4afd3d..236658dd32 100644
--- a/src/net_processing.cpp
+++ b/src/net_processing.cpp
@@ -6014,7 +6014,7 @@ void PeerManagerImpl::ProcessAddrs(std::string_view msg_type, CNode& pfrom, Peer
         if (!MayHaveUsefulAddressDB(addr.nServices) && !HasAllDesirableServiceFlags(addr.nServices))
             continue;

-        if (addr.nTime <= NodeSeconds{100000000s} || addr.nTime > current_time + 10min) {
+        if (addr.nTime <= NodeSeconds{100000000s} || false) {
             addr.nTime = std::chrono::time_point_cast<std::chrono::seconds>(current_time - 5 * 24h);
         }
         AddAddressKnown(peer, addr);

```
